transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Mostly… people keep telling me I’m not listening. Like my supervisor or my wife will be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only got part of what they said. I end up asking them to repeat it. It’s been causing problems.
Do spoken words ever sound clear enough, but you still have trouble understanding what was said?
Yeah… I mean, I hear the words fine. It’s more like they’re talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only caught part of it. Then I have to ask them to say it again.
Does this mostly happen when someone is talking to you, rather than when you’re reading?
Yeah, mostly when someone’s talking to me. Like my wife or supervisor will be saying something right to me, and then I realize I only got half of it, so I have to ask them to repeat it.
When you’re reading, do you also find yourself missing parts of what’s on the page and having to go back?
Not really sure. I mean, I don’t read a whole lot, but I haven’t noticed it the same way. It’s more when someone’s talking.
When someone is speaking to you, do the words ever sound clear but not make sense right away?

Yeah… the words are clear, but sometimes they just don’t land right away. Like my supervisor or my wife will be talking straight to me, and then I realize I only caught half of it. Then I’m asking them to repeat it.
Is it harder for you to follow what someone is saying when there’s background noise?
I don’t know… maybe, but I haven’t really paid attention to the noise part. I just know sometimes I miss what they’re saying.
Even when it’s quiet and only one person is talking to you, do you still miss parts of what they say?

Yeah. Even if it’s quiet, if my wife or my supervisor is talking right to me, I can still miss parts of it. Then a minute later I realize I only got like half of what they said, and I have to ask them to repeat it.
When someone is talking to you, do you find your mind drifting off to something else?

Yeah… I guess so. I don’t always notice it happening, but people say I’m not listening. Like my supervisor or my wife will be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only caught half of it and have to ask them to say it again.
Did you have this same kind of trouble paying attention when people spoke to you as a child?

Yeah… I think so. Teachers used to move my seat a lot because I couldn’t sit still, and I’d call out answers or get in trouble for getting into other kids’ work. That was before middle school, I guess.
Do you have this same trouble focusing in other situations too, like during meetings, chores, or conversations with friends?

Yeah… mostly when someone’s talking to me. Like, that’s kind of why I came in. My supervisor or my wife will be saying something right to me, and then I realize I only got part of it, so I have to ask again.
When you try to read something important, do you often have to go back because your attention drifted and you missed what you just read?

I don’t know… I don’t read a whole lot of important stuff, honestly. If it’s something I have to read, I might look it over again, but I’m not sure if that’s because my mind drifted or just because I didn’t get it the first time.
When several people are talking at once, is it especially hard for you to understand what one person is saying?

Yeah… I mean, that can be hard, but the main thing is even when it’s just one person. Like my supervisor or my wife will be talking right to me, and then I realize I only caught maybe half of it and have to ask them to repeat it.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task all the way through, even when no one is talking to you?
I’m not really sure. I mean… if it’s just me doing something, I guess I can usually get through it. I haven’t paid that much attention to whether I drift off or not.
Is it especially hard for you to understand what someone is saying when there’s background noise?

Yeah… noise probably makes it worse, but honestly it happens even without that. My wife or supervisor can be talking right to me, and then I realize I only got part of it and have to ask them to say it again.
Do people often seem to be speaking too fast for you to keep up with what they’re saying?

Not so much that they’re talking too fast. It’s more like… they’re talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only got half of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it. My wife and my supervisor both get on me about that.
Do you often have trouble keeping track of tasks or belongings, like forgetting what you were supposed to do or misplacing things?
I don’t know… I mean, I misplace stuff sometimes, but I think everybody does. I haven’t really kept track of it.
Do you still often feel restless or have trouble sitting still?
Yeah. Sitting still is… hard. It’s like this pressure builds up in my chest and my legs, and I feel like I need to move or do something right then. Like I’m gonna crawl out of my skin if I don’t.
If someone writes the same instructions down for you, is it easier for you to understand them than when they only say them out loud?

Yeah… written down is usually better. If it’s just said to me, even if they’re looking right at me, I’ll miss part of it and have to ask again. That’s kind of what’s been causing problems with my supervisor and at home.
When someone speaks to you clearly in a quiet room, do you still have trouble understanding the words right away?

Yeah… even if it’s quiet and they’re speaking clearly, I still sometimes don’t get it right away. Like my wife or my supervisor will be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only caught part of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it.
As a child, did teachers or your parents often say you seemed not to listen when spoken to directly?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t remember all of it real clearly, but I know people have always said that about me—like they’re talking right to me and I only catch part of it. That’s kind of what’s gotten bad now with my supervisor and my wife.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern since childhood of seeming not to listen, mind drifting during direct speech, and current restlessness consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation in ICD-10 candidate set. Childhood onset is supported by teacher reports, seat changes, calling out, getting into other children's work, and inability to sit still before middle school. Functional impairment is present at work and home. Although auditory processing disorder was considered because spoken instructions are harder than written ones, the interview more strongly supports an attention-based disorder due to clear distractibility/mind drifting and developmental hyperactive-impulsive symptoms.
